scenes.title: CodeArtifact Dependency Flow
scenes.narration: Follow the dependency hierarchy shown across the top. A CodeArtifact domain is a logical container for repositories, repositories store packages, and each package can have multiple published versions. The diagram shows approved dependencies originating in public upstream ecosystems such as PyPI or npm and being consumed through a private CodeArtifact repository. A developer's pip or npm client reads from that repository rather than fetching every dependency directly from an unreviewed public source. The same pattern applies to AWS CodeBuild, where reproducible builds install pinned package versions from the approved registry. The authentication path uses a short-lived CodeArtifact authorisation token, not a permanent credential committed to a build file. The build identity still needs the appropriate domain and repository permissions, and the package manager needs the correct repository endpoint and login configuration. Caching a public package in a private registry does not automatically make it secure; define upstream policy, vulnerability scanning, allowed versions and approval workflow. This architecture controls dependency distribution and supports software supply-chain governance.
